Quiet Metropolis

A series about the calm that sits inside the city. Shot from hillsides, waterfronts and open ground, these frames step back from the noise to look at the places we live as part of a larger landscape: dense rooftops spreading to the hills, a coastal town facing the sea, a skyline settling into blue-hour reflections, and a sun breaking through heavy cloud. Mostly in black and white, with a single deep-blue frame, the series is about light, distance and stillness.

In Passing

Everyday life moves through and rests inside the places we build. A gull cuts across a blurred wall of apartment blocks; a dog lies in the dust while a car blurs by. Using motion blur and selective color, the series sets the still against the fast, and asks which of them we really notice.

Stone Witnesses

The sculpted figures that stand guard over old churches and squares. Shot low against heavy clouds, in black and white, saints and angels become quiet observers of the changing world below them. The series is about weight, patience and the expressions that stone keeps long after the people who carved it are gone.

Held Notes

A quiet study of an instrument between performances. Shot close and in black and white, the series follows the grain of the wood, the line of the strings, the curve of the f-holes and the pages of music around them. Nothing is played here. The frames hold the moment before sound, when the instrument is all texture, shadow and possibility.
